items.title: Test-driven development with an LLM for fun and profit
items.raw_content: Welcome to the very first post in a new blog! Here I will discuss software development, SRE work, and other fun stuff. Sometimes an idea is just too good to pass up. I hope this blog will motivate me to turn sparks and little pieces into general knowledge in writing the words down. The other day I was discussing Tabby with a coworker. We talked about whether we should consider AI-autocompleted code harmful and ditch everyoneâs newfound habit due to LLMâs inherent unreliability and their tendency toward spaghetti code, throwing traditional software engineering principles like DRY out the window. I disagreed: what if we could have a framework that integrates AI development tooling while also making everything better and more reliable instead? This instantly reminds me of Test-Driven Development, or TDD, which I think is great when combined with the use of a Large Language Model.
items.title_zh: 用 LLM 实践测试驱动开发：既有趣又有收获
items.summary: The author argues that test-driven development offers a practical framework for using LLMs to write code, addressing concerns about AI-generated spaghetti code and unreliable autocompletion.

items.title: Build a Database in 3000 Lines with 0 Dependencies
items.raw_content: Complex software like databases, compilers, and browsers are treated like black boxes. You use them every day as a user , but you probably don’t understand them as a programmer , even though they are nothing but code. Why? But that doesn’t mean you can’t learn these things. People have built small, toy versions of these things for learning purposes, such as C in 4 Functions , Crafting Interpreters , Web Browser Engineering . It turns out that if you minimize uninteresting details and focus on the essentials, you can recreate seemingly complex software and learn its core ideas.

items.summary: The article argues that complex software like databases can be learned by rebuilding a minimal version, and presents a database implemented in 3,000 lines with zero dependencies.

items.title: Six day and IP address certificate options in 2025
items.raw_content: Update: January 15, 2026 Six-day and IP address certificates are now generally available. See 6-day and IP Address Certificates are Generally Available for details. This year we will continue to pursue our commitment to improving the security of the Web PKI by introducing the option to get certificates with six-day lifetimes (“short-lived certificates”). We will also add support for IP addresses in addition to domain names. Our longer-lived certificates, which currently have a lifetime of 90 days, will continue to be available alongside our six-day offering. Subscribers will be able to opt in to short-lived certificates via a certificate profile mechanism being added to our ACME API.

items.title: Bunkers in Albania
items.raw_content: Concrete military bunkers ( Albanian : bunkerët ) are a ubiquitous sight in Albania , where more than 170,000 bunkers were built by the Hoxhaist government from the 1960s to the 1980s. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] This is an average of 5.7 bunkers for every square kilometer. Hoxha 's program of "bunkerization" ( bunkerizimi ) resulted in the construction of bunkers in every corner of the then- People's Socialist Republic of Albania , ranging from mountain passes to city streets. They were never used for their intended purpose during the years that Hoxha governed. The cost of constructing them was a drain on Albania's resources, diverting them away from dealing with the country's housing shortage and poor roads.
items.title_zh: 阿尔巴尼亚的地堡
items.summary: More than 170,000 concrete bunkers were built across Albania from the 1960s to the 1980s, an average of 5.7 per square kilometer, at a cost that drained national resources.

items.title: Coded Deep Learning: Framework and Algorithm
items.raw_content:
Authors: En-hui Yang, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi

The success of deep learning (DL) is often achieved with large models and high complexity during both training and post-training inferences, hindering training in resource-limited settings. To alleviate these issues, this paper introduces a new framework dubbed ``coded deep learning'' (CDL), which integrates information-theoretic coding concepts into the inner workings of DL, to significantly compress model weights and activations, reduce computational complexity at both training and post-training inference stages, and enable efficient model/data parallelism. Specifically, within CDL, (i) we first propose a novel probabilistic method for quantizing both model weights and activations, and its soft differentiable variant which offers an analytic formula for gradient calculation during training; (ii) both the forward and backward passes during training are executed over quantized weights and activations, eliminating most floating-point operations and reducing training complexity; (iii) during training, both weights and activations are entropy constrained so that they are compressible in an information-theoretic sense throughout training, thus reducing communication costs in model/data parallelism; and (iv) the trained model in CDL is by default in a quantized format with compressible quantized weights, reducing post-training inference and storage complexity. Additionally, a variant of CDL, namely relaxed CDL (R-CDL), is presented to further improve the trade-off between validation accuracy and compression though requiring full precision in training with other advantageous features of CDL intact. Extensive empirical results show that CDL and R-CDL outperform the state-of-the-art algorithms in DNN compression in the literature.
items.title_zh: Coded Deep Learning：框架与算法
items.summary: The paper introduces coded deep learning, a framework that brings information-theoretic coding into model training to compress weights and activations, cut computation and support efficient parallelism. It also presents a relaxed variant and reports gains over state-of-the-art DNN compression methods.

items.title: From Explainability to Interpretability: Interpretable Policies in Reinforcement Learning Via Model Explanation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Peilang Li, Umer Siddique, Yongcan Cao

Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has shown remarkable success in complex domains, however, the inherent black box nature of deep neural network policies raises significant challenges in understanding and trusting the decision-making processes. While existing explainable RL methods provide local insights, they fail to deliver a global understanding of the model, particularly in high-stakes applications. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel model-agnostic approach that bridges the gap between explainability and interpretability by leveraging Shapley values to transform complex deep RL policies into transparent representations. The proposed approach offers two key contributions: a novel approach employing Shapley values to policy interpretation beyond local explanations and a general framework applicable to off-policy and on-policy algorithms. We evaluate our approach with three existing deep RL algorithms and validate its performance in two classic control environments. The results demonstrate that our approach not only preserves the original models' performance but also generates more stable interpretable policies.
items.title_zh: 从可解释性到可理解性：通过模型解释获得强化学习中的可解释策略
items.summary: The authors propose a model-agnostic method that uses Shapley values to turn deep reinforcement learning policies into transparent, interpretable representations. Evaluated on three RL algorithms in two control environments, it preserved original performance while producing more stable policies.

items.title: An LLM-Guided Tutoring System for Social Skills Training
items.raw_content:
Authors: Michael Guevarra, Indronil Bhattacharjee, Srijita Das, Christabel Wayllace, Carrie Demmans Epp et al.

Social skills training targets behaviors necessary for success in social interactions. However, traditional classroom training for such skills is often insufficient to teach effective communication -- one-to-one interaction in real-world scenarios is preferred to lecture-style information delivery. This paper introduces a framework that allows instructors to collaborate with large language models to dynamically design realistic scenarios for students to communicate. Our framework uses these scenarios to enable student rehearsal, provide immediate feedback, and visualize performance for both students and instructors. Unlike traditional intelligent tutoring systems, instructors can easily co-create scenarios with a large language model without technical skills. Additionally, the system generates new scenario branches in real time when existing options do not fit the student's response.
items.title_zh: 面向社交技能训练的 LLM 引导式辅导系统
items.summary: The paper presents a framework in which instructors work with large language models to design realistic social skills scenarios, let students rehearse them, and receive immediate feedback. It can also generate new scenario branches in real time and requires no technical skills from instructors.

items.title: ASTRA: A Scene-aware TRAnsformer-based model for trajectory prediction
items.raw_content:
Authors: Izzeddin Teeti, Aniket Thomas, Munish Monga, Sachin Kumar, Uddeshya Singh et al.

We present ASTRA (A} Scene-aware TRAnsformer-based model for trajectory prediction), a light-weight pedestrian trajectory forecasting model that integrates the scene context, spatial dynamics, social inter-agent interactions and temporal progressions for precise forecasting. We utilised a U-Net-based feature extractor, via its latent vector representation, to capture scene representations and a graph-aware transformer encoder for capturing social interactions. These components are integrated to learn an agent-scene aware embedding, enabling the model to learn spatial dynamics and forecast the future trajectory of pedestrians. The model is designed to produce both deterministic and stochastic outcomes, with the stochastic predictions being generated by incorporating a Conditional Variational Auto-Encoder (CVAE). ASTRA also proposes a simple yet effective weighted penalty loss function, which helps to yield predictions that outperform a wide array of state-of-the-art deterministic and generative models. ASTRA demonstrates an average improvement of 27%/10% in deterministic/stochastic settings on the ETH-UCY dataset, and 26% improvement on the PIE dataset, respectively, along with seven times fewer parameters than the existing state-of-the-art model (see Figure 1). Additionally, the model's versatility allows it to generalize across different perspectives, such as Bird's Eye View (BEV) and Ego-Vehicle View (EVV).
items.title_zh: ASTRA：面向轨迹预测的场景感知 Transformer 模型
items.summary: ASTRA is a lightweight pedestrian trajectory prediction model that combines scene context, spatial dynamics, social interactions and temporal progression using a U-Net feature extractor and a graph-aware transformer. It reports 27%/10% average improvement on ETH-UCY, 26% on PIE and seven times fewer parameters than the prior state of the art.

items.title: Semi-Supervised Image-Based Narrative Extraction: A Case Study with Historical Photographic Records
items.raw_content:
Authors: Fausto German, Brian Keith, Mauricio Matus, Diego Urrutia, Claudio Meneses

This paper presents a semi-supervised approach to extracting narratives from historical photographic records using an adaptation of the narrative maps algorithm. We extend the original unsupervised text-based method to work with image data, leveraging deep learning techniques for visual feature extraction and similarity computation. Our method is applied to the ROGER dataset, a collection of photographs from the 1928 Sacambaya Expedition in Bolivia captured by Robert Gerstmann. We compare our algorithmically extracted visual narratives with expert-curated timelines of varying lengths (5 to 30 images) to evaluate the effectiveness of our approach. In particular, we use the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) algorithm to match the extracted narratives with the expert-curated baseline. In addition, we asked an expert on the topic to qualitatively evaluate a representative example of the resulting narratives. Our findings show that the narrative maps approach generally outperforms random sampling for longer timelines (10+ images, p < 0.05), with expert evaluation confirming the historical accuracy and coherence of the extracted narratives. This research contributes to the field of computational analysis of visual cultural heritage, offering new tools for historians, archivists, and digital humanities scholars to explore and understand large-scale image collections. The method's ability to generate meaningful narratives from visual data opens up new possibilities for the study and interpretation of historical events through photographic evidence.
items.title_zh: 基于图像的半监督叙事提取：历史照片档案案例研究
items.summary: The authors adapt a narrative maps algorithm to historical photographs, using deep learning for visual features and similarity, and apply it to the ROGER dataset from a 1928 Bolivian expedition. The approach outperformed random sampling for timelines of 10 or more images, with expert review supporting the narratives' historical accuracy.

items.title: Learning Noisy Halfspaces with a Margin: Massart is No Harder than Random
items.raw_content:
Authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Vasilis Kontonis, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Kevin Tian

We study the problem of PAC learning $γ$-margin halfspaces with Massart noise. We propose a simple proper learning algorithm, the Perspectron, that has sample complexity $\widetilde{O}((εγ)^{-2})$ and achieves classification error at most $η+ε$ where $η$ is the Massart noise rate. Prior works [DGT19,CKMY20] came with worse sample complexity guarantees (in both $ε$ and $γ$) or could only handle random classification noise [DDK+23,KIT+23] -- a much milder noise assumption. We also show that our results extend to the more challenging setting of learning generalized linear models with a known link function under Massart noise, achieving a similar sample complexity to the halfspace case. This significantly improves upon the prior state-of-the-art in this setting due to [CKMY20], who introduced this model.
items.title_zh: 带间隔的噪声半空间学习：Massart 噪声并不比随机噪声更难
items.summary: The paper proposes Perspectron, a proper learning algorithm for PAC learning margin halfspaces under Massart noise with sample complexity O~((epsilon gamma)^-2) and error at most eta plus epsilon. The results are shown to extend to generalized linear models with a known link function.
